text:
hana: Quick flag — Dockline's LoRA merge into redwood-v2.2 produced a weird token-shift where the model suddenly treats token id 50256 as a high-prob suffix. Repro steps and a short diff below — pinging @omar for merge script + @glee for mapping checks.

omar: can you share numbers and how you merged?

hana: short numbers from a 30-example smoke: median_len dropped 19 -> 8, top1_eos_prob at pos2 jumped 0.03 -> 0.71, embed_cosine(base vs merged) 0.986 -> 0.947. Merge command: `python tools/merge_lora.py --base models/redwood/v2.2 --lora dockline_v1.safetensors --out /tmp/dock-merged.safetensors` (default fold-to-fp16).

glee: did you compare runtime-apply (adapter) vs merged?

hana: yes — runtime adapter path is fine. The oddity appears only on the merged artifact. I ran a tiny param map check and found several LoRA keys mapping to the wte slice unexpectedly. Short excerpt:

```
# mapping_report.txt (dry-run)
lo_ra.keys: ['embed_proj_0', 'layer5.mlp.down', 'lm_head_delta']
applied_mappings:
  embed_proj_0 -> wte.weight[0:1024]
  layer5.mlp.down -> transformer.h.5.mlp.fc1.weight
  lm_head_delta -> lm_head.weight
```

hana: notice embed_proj_0 mapping — Dockline's LoRA used a vendor key name that our conversion heuristics interpreted as embedding projector. But runtime-apply preserves keys and applies by explicit registry so it went to the intended layer. The merged writer however applied to the token embedding slice.

omar: ah — mapping heuristic bug. Two issues then: 1) misapplied delta into embeddings, 2) fold-to-fp16 changes sharpness. Which is bigger?

hana: both matter. After forcing `--preserve-fp32` the metrics improved: median_len 16 and eos_prob 0.12, embed_cosine 0.973. After correcting the mapping (explicit mapping JSON) and merging (fp32 preserve) we get near-baseline: median_len 18, eos_prob 0.05, embed_cosine 0.985.

glee: good. What's the fix plan?

omar: immediate: add a strict mapping pass in merge_lora.py that rejects ambiguous vendor keys and requires an explicit map file for nonstandard key patterns. Second: change default to preserve-fp32 for merges that touch token embedding or lm_head. Third: add a post-merge sanity check that asserts mean-abs-diff for wte.weight < 0.005 and lm_head < 0.01, otherwise fail and produce mapping_report.txt.

hana: I also recommend adding a small CI test that simulates vendor key ambiguity (one LoRA with keys like 'embed_proj_0' and ensure merge fails without explicit map). I can open the unit test.

ops-bot: queued job 1791112250: re-merge with explicit map and preserve-fp32 -> quantize(int8) -> quick-eval.

eval-bot: job 1791112250 completed: metrics: median_len 18, top3_mass 0.37 (base 0.36), embed_cosine 0.985. Logs: https://internal/evals/1791112250

glee: perfect. Also add onboarding doc note: require vendors to include a mapping-json when LoRA keys are not identical to our canonical layer names. Provide a tiny template snippet.

omar: I'll push a PR to tools/merge_lora.py to add the mapping guard, default preserve-fp32 for critical params, and include the mapping_report output.

hana: I've dropped the 10-example mini-evalpack + mapping_report into the customer ticket and asked Dockline to sign off before we publish merged artifact. Blocking until they confirm.

glee: tl;dr: root cause = vendor key-name ambiguity causing LoRA deltas to be applied to embeddings + fp16 folding worsened softmax sharpness. Mitigations: explicit mapping, preserve-fp32 default for merges touching embeddings/lm_head, post-merge guards, CI test, and a vendor mapping template.

omar: thanks team. I'll follow up on the PR and the CI test.

hana: thanks all — will update here after Dockline signs off. :white_check_mark:
